motivation: Miyasaka first demonstrated (2009) that organometal halide perovskites act as light absorbers in solar cells. Park (2012) and Snaith (2012) then turned them into solid-state thin-film devices, and Snaith showed that the perovskite itself carries both electrons and holes over long distances. This established a new class of solution-processable semiconductors. Their strong absorption, defect tolerance, long carrier diffusion lengths and tunable band gap overturned the idea that high-efficiency photovoltaics require ultra-pure crystalline materials. Power conversion efficiencies went from about 4% to above 26% in single junctions, and perovskite–silicon tandems now exceed 34%, beyond the silicon limit. The discovery opened a broad field of physics on ionic–electronic transport, polarons and interfaces, and it has spread to LEDs, detectors and lasers. Commercial tandem modules are emerging, which makes this a discovery of great benefit to humanity in the sense Nobel intended.
